newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN says 2,000 killed by Rwandan army since May.
newsitem.headline: UN says 2,000 killed by Rwandan army since May.

text.p: More than 2,000 people, mostly unarmed civilians, have been killed in a troubled northwestern Rwanda region during army operations in May and June, the United Nations human rights office said on Friday.

In a report released in Geneva, it said the killings in Ruhengeri, a predominantly Hutu area where the Tutsi-dominated army is fighting a rebellion, were a record high for any two-month reporting period in the central African country.

The Geneva-based U.N. rights centre said it was alarmed by Rwandan Patriotic Army (RPA) operations in Ruhengeri, which were launched in response to rebel attacks but resulted in the deaths of civilians including many elderly, women and children.
"The government of Rwanda should take steps to prevent the excessive use of force by the security forces, including the RPA," it said.

The report followed one released by the London-based human rights group Amnesty International, which alleged on Thursday that more than 2,300 unarmed Rwandan civilians were killed in May, June and July. It accused the international community of ignoring the slaughter.
The U.N. human rights office said the Rwandan government, which is dominated by minority Tutsis, rejected its findings on the killings and suggested conducting joint investigations.
